Visioner BIG | 🇺🇦 🇸🇪 🇷🇺 ‼️ ‼️ Ukraine could receive Swedish Gripen fighter jets as early as January, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, potentially strengthening Kyiv’s ability to counter Russian aircraft launching guided aerial bombs. Zelenskyy said the fighters would help Ukrainian forces intercept Russian Sukhoi aircraft used to deploy guided aerial bombs, commonly known as KABs. These weapons have become a major threat to Ukrainian frontline positions and cities. The number of Gripens expected and the precise delivery schedule have not been specified in the reported remarks. Gripen fighters could improve Ukraine’s ability to challenge Russian aviation near the front, particularly aircraft launching glide bombs from a distance. Their effectiveness will depend on available air-to-air missiles, pilot training, and operational support. Bringing Russian bomb carriers under greater threat could help reduce the pressure on Ukrainian ground forces. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

Visioner BREAKING | 🇷🇺 🇺🇦 ‼️ ‼️ More than 720,000 Russian troops may have been killed or gone missing in Ukraine, according to a new assessment attributed to independent Russian outlets Mediazona and Meduza, based on allegedly leaked Russian state statistics. The reported analysis of hacked Rosstat databases identifies approximately 520,000 Russian servicemen recorded as dead, alongside more than 200,000 listed as missing. The dataset reportedly ends in September 2026 and excludes several categories of foreign fighters and personnel from Russian-backed formations in occupied Ukraine. Separately, estimates cited in the report suggest more than 900,000 Russian troops have been seriously wounded and removed from combat, bringing the claimed combined total of dead, missing, and severely wounded to over 1.6 million. These extraordinary figures have not been independently verified, and missing personnel cannot automatically be counted as confirmed deaths. If substantiated, the figures would reveal an enormous human cost of Russia’s invasion and raise serious questions about the sustainability of its military manpower. However, the distinction between confirmed deaths, missing soldiers, and severe injuries is essential when assessing the actual scale of Russian losses. Russia’s embassy to Germany has refuted what it called baseless allegations in the German media about Russia’s space activities. “We categorically reject all these groundless allegations regarding Russia’s space activities. They're out of touch with reality and are part of a propaganda campaign aimed at smearing Russia and its initiatives to prevent an arms race in outer space,” the embassy told TASS. “Our country's steps to explore and develop outer space are being taken in accordance with international obligations, solely for peaceful purposes, and do not threaten other countries’ activities in outer space. Russia strictly adheres to the fundamental 1967 Outer Space Treaty,” it stressed, adding that for decades, Russia “has been making a significant contribution to keeping outer space free of weapons of any kind and preventing it from becoming yet another arena of tension and armed confrontation.”
